title: Sensex Surges 695 Points as Nifty Reclaims 23,000 on IT Rally
excerpt: Indian benchmarks rebounded on Wednesday, October 21, with Infosys and TCS leading an earnings-driven IT rally after Monday's sharp sell-off.
body:
• The Sensex opened at 74,337.93, up 485 points, and climbed as much as 695 points to 74,548 in early trade on Wednesday, October 21, according to IANS.
  • The Nifty opened at 23,016, up 127 points, and touched 23,086, with the Nifty IT index rising about 2 per cent as Infosys gained 2.47 per cent and TCS 2.08 per cent.
  • Foreign investors sold about Rs 1,148 crore of equities on October 19 while domestic institutions bought about Rs 3,200 crore, IANS reported.
  • For NRI investors: the rally was earnings- and IT-led after Monday's 876-point Sensex fall, so index levels near 23,150-23,200 are the resistance traders are watching, per BusinessLine market coverage.

Indian equities rebounded sharply on Wednesday, October 21, with the Sensex surging as much as 695 points and the Nifty reclaiming 23,000 in early trade, led by information technology shares and heavyweights including Reliance Industries, Infosys and TCS, according to Upstox's market report. As of 9:24 am, the Sensex was up 672 points at 74,525 and the Nifty had advanced 180 points to 23,075.

IANS reported the Sensex opened at 74,337.93, up 485.03 points or 0.66 per cent from its previous close of 73,852.90, while the Nifty opened at 23,016, up 127.05 points. Sector gauges for IT, PSU banks, cement and oil and gas rose up to 1.97 per cent, while media and chemicals traded lower.

IT leads, Bajaj Finance lags

Infosys led the Nifty gainers, rising 2.47 per cent, followed by TCS at 2.08 per cent and UltraTech Cement at 1.96 per cent. Bajaj Finance was the biggest loser, down 2.32 per cent, with Bajaj Finserv off 0.49 per cent. The Hindu BusinessLine's live coverage noted the IT index jumped 2.2 per cent, with L&T Technology Services surging 10.5 per cent after reporting September-quarter revenue and profit growth, before the benchmarks pared some early gains by mid-morning.

Global cues and flows

Asian markets traded higher following Wall Street gains, as early corporate earnings bolstered confidence, Reuters reported via Upstox. Japan's Nikkei rose 1.23 per cent, Taiwan's weighted index gained 1.8 per cent and South Korea's KOSPI surged 3.76 per cent, while China's Shanghai Composite eased 0.17 per cent. Overnight, the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 1.02 per cent and the S&P 500 gained 0.28 per cent, while the Nasdaq slipped 0.02 per cent and oil prices eased.

Flows remain a counterweight. In the previous session, foreign institutional investors were net sellers of about Rs 1,148 crore, while domestic institutions bought about Rs 3,200 crore, according to IANS. Monday's sell-off had pushed the Nifty down 257 points and lifted India VIX 5.33 per cent to 14.7725, a sign of elevated caution.

What to watch

Analysts cited by IANS said elevated Brent crude and US bond yields keep a sell-on-rally structure in place near term, but improving earnings growth, fair large-cap valuations and strong domestic liquidity should support the market on declines, with IT and banking — both solid in the second quarter — likely to see domestic accumulation on corrections. BusinessLine put immediate Nifty resistance at 23,150-23,200 and support at 22,800. For diaspora investors tracking Indian portfolios from abroad, the session's message is narrow: this was an earnings-led IT bounce inside a still-cautious tape, and second-quarter results, crude and India-US trade developments will set the next leg.
